title: Security review - pen test results & patching cadence - Orion Bank
next_steps: Redwood to send redacted pen test report and remediation tracker
Schedule technical deep dive with Orion infra (w/ logs and kernel-level notes)
Share SOC 2 Type 2 report and compliance artifact links
Provide patching cadence and CVE response SLA doc
action_items: Samira Patel - Send redacted pen test report and remediation spreadsheet - due 2026-04-10
Ethan Ng - Schedule deep dive and collect traces for two failing test cases - due 2026-04-14
Lina Zhao (Orion) - Share current patching window and change freeze dates - due 2026-04-09
Markus Reilly (Orion) - Provide list of prioritized assets and data residency requirements - due 2026-04-12
summary: Review of recent third-party penetration test results, discussion of vulnerability remediation prioritization, confirmation of secure SDLC and patching cadence, and alignment on next steps for SOC2 artifacts and a technical deep dive.
transcript:
[00:00:00] Samira (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I see folks from Orion on, thanks. We planned 45 minutes, so we'll run through the pen test findings, remediation plan, and then cover patching cadence and SDLC questions.
[00:00:18] Markus (Orion - Head of Security): Yep, thanks Samira. Appreciate you fitting this in. We got the initial pen test from SecureNorth last week and had some follow-ups. High level we'd like to confirm timelines and what changes if any to production deployment processes.
[00:00:35] Ethan (Redwood SE): Hi all, Ethan here. I'll walk through the technical findings at a high level, call out the three items that tripped SecureNorth as critical or high, and then we can talk mitigation strategies.
[00:00:48] Lina (Orion - DevOps): Quick clarification, are we talking about Redwood hosted environment or our private VPC deployment? A few of the findings reference network exposure.
[00:00:58] Samira: Good call out. This is for the Redwood Dedicated cluster provisioned in Orion's AWS account under the VPC peering setup; so it's the private deployment with customer-managed networking.
[00:01:12] Priya (Orion - Legal): For context, some of our regulators will require proof of patching cadence and the SLA for CVE response for any third-party vendor processing customer data.
[00:01:22] Samira: Understood. We'll make sure to include the patching cadence doc and our SOC2 artifacts in the follow-up.
[00:01:28] Ethan: Ok, jumping in. Finding one, marked critical, was an out-of-date OS package on the inference nodes that allowed privilege escalation in a specific container image used in the runtime. The pen test showed proof-of-concept local privilege escalation.
[00:01:45] Jonas (Orion - Platform): That was the alpine variant on some worker nodes, right? We patched our image last month, but looks like a leftover image was present in the cluster.
[00:01:54] Ethan: Correct. The report indicates a stale image, and SecureNorth flagged it as critical because of how the container was launched in one of the test scenarios.
[00:02:05] Markus: Is this something on Redwood's build pipeline or on our side? Who controls image churn?
[00:02:12] Carlos (CSM): I can clarify — for Dedicated, Redwood provides the base runtime images and we push updates; Orion's cluster runs those images but Orion controls node-level patching. So it's a shared responsibility.
[00:02:26] Mark-ish (mis-attributed Speaker 6): mm-hmm, shared of course, yeah.
[00:02:29] Ethan: Right, we handle updates to the runtime and publish patched images. The orchestration to replace nodes is in the customer's infra; sometimes old images linger if a node wasn't drained properly.
[00:02:40] Lina: That checks out. Our automation didn't rotate one ASG after the last deploy. We have a playbook to replace nodes but we missed one.
[00:02:48] Samira: Action item there — we'll add an end-to-end checklist to the handoff docs and include node rotation verification.
[00:02:56] [00:03:00] Ethan: Finding two, high severity: insufficiently protected KMS key access for a service account in one region; the pen tester found overly permissive IAM bindings that could allow key usage from an unintended principal.
[00:03:14] Markus: That's the thing we care most about — keys and encryption. Do you have exact principals listed in the report?
[00:03:20] Samira: We'll send the redacted report; it includes the principals. To summarize, Redwood's runtime uses Orion-managed KMS keys when configured, and sometimes our automation created a role binding during onboarding that didn't get tightened to a least-privilege principal.
[00:03:36] Priya: Our compliance team will insist on evidence of key separation and audit logs. Does Redwood provide key-use audit trails?
[00:03:44] Ethan: Yes — when using Orion KMS, CloudTrail logs show Encrypt/Decrypt and DescribeKey calls. We also surface those events in the Redwood Console's audit logs if you enable the integration. There was a note in the report that the key access wasn't scoped to the specific service account — so remediation is straightforward: tighten IAM and rotate the keys.
[00:03:59] Lina: How fast can we rotate keys without causing downtime? We have sessions with long token TTLs.
[00:04:06] Ethan: We recommend rolling key rotation with the typical TTL overlap: create new key, update service to use new key, then schedule decommission. We can provide scripts to automate rotation to avoid downtime.
[00:04:17] Markus: Ok. Critical timeline question — SecureNorth recommended 30 days for critical remediation. Is that feasible?
[00:04:25] Samira: For the KMS IAM tightening and node rotation, yes 30 days is reasonable. For code-level fixes or kernel patches which require coordination across teams, it can vary.
[00:04:35] [00:04:40] Ethan: Finding three was medium — information leakage via verbose debug endpoints enabled in a staging path. Not accessible externally but found via internal discovery.
[00:04:51] Jonas: That was from a debug flag in an older build of the admin UI, we can flip that off quickly.
[00:04:56] Samira: Great. That's low friction.
[00:05:00] Priya: Can you clarify how Redwood manages secure SDLC? We need to include that in our vendor risk review.
[00:05:07] Ethan: Sure. High level: Redwood enforces code review, CI run for all PRs including SAST and dependency scanning, has a release gating process that requires passing tests and manual approval for infra changes, and maintains a vulnerability triage board.
[00:05:24] Samira: We also do periodic dependency upgrades and have a scheduled quarterly dependency audit; we can share the policy doc.
[00:05:29] Markus: Do you require developers to remediate critical findings from SAST before release?
[00:05:34] Ethan: Yes, critical SAST findings must be fixed or mitigated before merge; our policy forces CI to fail on those classes. Medium findings get SLA'd into the backlog depending on risk.
[00:05:44] Lina: About patching cadence — our compliance needs a formal cadence and emergency patch window. What's Redwood's typical cadence for runtime security patches?
[00:05:53] Samira: For hosted and dedicated workloads, we publish security patch bulletins monthly; critical CVEs trigger an out-of-band patch within 72 hours for the Redwood-managed images. For customer-managed nodes we coordinate and provide patched images and a playbook.
[00:06:08] Lina: So for Orion, we would get a patched image and then the rotation would be our responsibility.
[00:06:13] Ethan: Correct. We can offer assistance via runbook and we can also provide a temporary emergency patching engagement if you want us to coordinate node replacement with your infra team.
[00:06:23] Markus: That's helpful. We may want Redwood to coordinate the initial remediation to reduce risk.
[00:06:29] Carlos: We can do a concierge run for the first rotation as part of the Dedicated onboarding package, it's documented in our support addendum.
[00:06:36] [00:06:40] Priya: On audit logs — regulators want tamper-evident logs and retention for 7 years in some cases. What does Redwood store versus what stays in our CloudTrail?
[00:06:50] Ethan: We capture request/response metadata and user actions in the Redwood Console logs; for Dedicated deployments, the canonical cloud-level audit logs (CloudTrail) remain in Orion's account. We can stream a copy to Orion's S3 or a GCS bucket for long-term retention; we also offer log signing and export options.
[00:07:08] Markus: Good. Also data residency — some EU customers require data never to leave the EU region. Does the Redwood runtime support region pinning?
[00:07:16] Samira: Yes, region pinning is supported in Dedicated. You can pin model execution to a particular region and we ensure the inference runtime and any temporary caches live in that region. We'll include the architecture diagram showing data flow.
[00:07:29] Lina: What about KV cache and any temporary storage? Are they encrypted at rest by default?
[00:07:35] Ethan: Yes, KV cache and local disk are encrypted; if you're using customer-managed keys we use the same KMS for disk encryption. There was a note in the pen test that one cache snapshot was accessible because of a misconfigured IAM role — that's the KMS binding issue we discussed.
[00:07:49] [00:07:55] Samira: On the topic of RBAC and SSO — does Orion plan to use SAML SSO? We support SAML and OIDC.
[00:08:03] Markus: We use SAML with our IdP. We want RBAC controls to map to our internal teams so that only DevOps and Security can perform node rotation and key management.
[00:08:13] Ethan: We can map SAML groups to Redwood roles; we also have fine-grained RBAC in the Console for runbooks, audit logs, and key rotation permissions. We'll send the role mapping doc.
[00:08:23] Priya: For our procurement checklist, can you provide a sample admin role mapping and a whitelist of admin IPs?
[00:08:29] Samira: Yes, will include sample IAM and role mappings and IP allowlist doc.
[00:08:33] [00:08:40] Markus: Back to vulnerability management — what's Redwood's SLA for triaging and patching vulnerabilities that affect the runtime?
[00:08:47] Samira: We have internal SLAs: critical vulnerabilities are triaged within 24 hours and patches are published within 72 hours, with backports prioritized. Medium severity within 30 days. We'll include those SLAs.
[00:08:59] Lina: Do you run managed WAF or runtime detection?
[00:09:04] Ethan: We provide runtime anomaly detection and integrate with WAFs but WAF is typically in customer perimeter. We do have runtime protection that alerts on anomalous model input patterns and high request rates.
[00:09:16] [00:09:20] Jonas: A nit — on the pen test there was a mention of side-channel timing on the model serving path. Is that something you actively mitigate?
[00:09:27] Ethan: We've applied constant-time primitives in sensitive code paths and we recommend co-tenancy isolation and per-customer model instances where needed. We'll follow up with the exact mitigations applied to the runtime.
[00:09:40] Samira: Great. Let's recap the immediate next steps. We'll: 1) Send the redacted SecureNorth report and remediation tracker, 2) Share SOC2 Type 2 artifacts and role mapping docs, 3) Provide patched images and rotation runbook, 4) Schedule a technical deep dive to walk through two failing cases.
[00:10:01] Markus: That works. For the deep dive, we want to include our infra and secops, and ideally you can share the test harness or reproduction steps from SecureNorth.
[00:10:11] Ethan: We'll pull reproduction steps into a staging playbook, scrubbed for PII, and attach traces.
[00:10:18] Priya: Legal will need a redacted version of the full report for vendor risk.
[00:10:22] Samira: Understood. We'll redact and provide an attestation letter summarizing remediations once complete.
[00:10:29] [00:10:35] Markus: One last question — if we discover a critical zero-day, what's the emergency response process?
[00:10:41] Samira: We have an incident response runbook: 24x7 pager for security incidents, a communication timeline, customer notification within 2 hours for critical incidents, and a coordinated patch and rollback plan. We'll include the IR summary.
[00:10:56] Lina: Good to hear.
[00:11:00] Ethan: I'll note the specific things to include in the deep dive: kernel-level CVE patches applied, exact IAM principals in question, and the node rotation checklist.
[00:11:09] Samira: Ok I'll capture the action items. Carlos, anything on support or billing for the concierge rotation?
[00:11:15] Carlos: We'll cover the initial concierge rotation under onboarding credits; ongoing support is under the Dedicated support tier. We'll follow up in writing.
[00:11:23] [00:11:30] Markus: Thanks everyone. Appreciate clear timelines. We'll aim for initial remediation within 30 days and schedule the deep dive next week.
[00:11:38] Samira: Thanks all. We'll send the artifacts and a calendar invite for the deep dive.
[00:11:45] Speaker 6: thanks bye.
[00:11:50] Samira: Bye.

Note: transcript occasionally shows generically labeled speakers where the call system misattributed audio; details above map to attendees list. The full pen test PDF and remediation tracker will be shared via secure link; no sensitive PII included in the transcript.
